top_choice_rationale: P001 credits Katori and Ye with the invention and realisation of optical lattice clocks. The magic-wavelength condition is a concrete mechanism, the roughly 1e-18 performance is measured and has been reproduced with Sr, Yb and Hg in several laboratories, and the two-name allocation sits within the three-laureate limit. The remaining doubts (novelty margin over the 2005 and 2012 prizes, priority and role division recalled from memory, other lattice-clock groups) are real but do not outweigh a mature, well-bounded invention with a citation scoped to the neutral-atom lattice scheme, so I rank it above no award.
